subject: Docsprint — prompt collection & eval action plan
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>
To: Claire Novak <claire@docsprint.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Docsprint — prompt collection & eval action plan

Hi Claire — great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single thread for the data handoff and eval plan.

Recap (30 min call):
- Use case: customer support automation + smart triage for Docsprint’s enterprise customers (inbound tickets + knowledge base search).
- Priority signals: recall of KB, avoidance of hallucinations on policy/contract language, and safe handling of PII.
- Target latency: p95 generation latency < 250ms for short responses (<= 120 tokens) for live chat; higher latency acceptable for async summarization flows.

What we need from you to start the model-fit evals:
1) Representative prompt set (customer utterances): ~500–1,500 anonymized utterances across categories (billing, onboarding, config, escalation). Prefer a CSV with columns: conversation_id, user_text, conversation_context_tags.
2) Edge-case examples: ~50 examples where KB lookup fails, or user provides legal/PII content. Mark which items can stay in the dataset and which must be redacted.
3) A short note on redaction rules you prefer (we'll follow them exactly): e.g., remove full SSNs, mask partial account numbers, preserve product IDs.

Our recommended starting models for benchmarking (cost vs quality tradeoffs):
- Llama-2-13B (quantized) — good baseline for recall and lower cost.
- Falcon-40B-instruct (fp16) — higher quality for complex instruction following; higher cost.
- Redwood-optimized-7B (low-latency build) — if latency is critical for live chat flows.

We’ll run a small eval suite measuring: exact-match on KB retrieval snippets, hallucination rate (manual spot-check + automated hallucination heuristics), F1 for entity extraction when applicable, and latency (p50/p95). We’ll share a benchmark pack link once the data is uploaded.

Attachments: prompt_capture_template.csv (CSV template), sample_conversation_redacted.json (example redacted export).

Ask: can you confirm by EOD Wednesday (Dec 2) whether you can share the initial CSV and edge-case set? If you prefer, we can accept a staged upload (start with 200 rows) and iterate.

Thanks — next step after we receive data is a 1-week smoke eval and a short results call to review model recommendations.

Best,
Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
https://redwood.com | (415) 555-0191

Quick answers:
- We can share an initial batch of ~300 rows by Wed (Dec 2) and the full 1,200 set by next Friday (Dec 10).
- Redaction: we can pre-redact names and full SSNs. We prefer to keep product IDs and masked account numbers (e.g., acct: ****1234).
- Security: all files will be uploaded to the secure SFTP you provided (please send upload creds). We need to confirm where logs will be stored.

Attaching: docsprint_sample_prompts.csv (300 rows, redacted) and a short internal doc describing our redaction rules.

Questions from our side:
1) Do you have a recommended baseline evaluation script we can run locally before upload?
2) Is it possible to have an initial sanity check (no cost) against the Redwood-optimized-7B to make sure the format works?

We’re happy to sign an NDA if needed — I can send DocuSign today.

Best,
Claire Novak
Head of Product, Docsprint Solutions
claire@docsprint.ai

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>
To: Claire Novak <claire@docsprint.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Docsprint — prompt collection & eval action plan

Claire — perfect, thanks for the sample CSV and the redaction notes. A few clarifications and what we’ll do next: 

1) Quick onboarding checklist we’ll run once files land:
   - Verify file schema against prompt_capture_template.csv and report back format errors.
   - Run automated redaction validator to confirm no obvious PII leaks (SSN patterns, credit card regex).
   - Sanity-run the CSV through Redwood-optimized-7B to confirm parsing/encoding and send a small snapshot of outputs.

2) Baseline eval plan (what we’ll run during the 1-week smoke run):
   - Metrics: KB recall @K=5, hallucination rate (manual + model-based detection), entity F1 for billing references, response length distribution, latency p50/p95, and cost per 1k tokens.
   - We’ll surface failing prompt buckets (e.g., ambiguous KB references, legal language, PII redaction misses) and annotate examples for your team to review.

3) Model recommendations (finalized after smoke run) — initial guidance:
   - Live chat (low latency): Redwood-optimized-7B (quant) or a tuned 13B quantized variant for balance of quality and latency.
   - Complex policy/legal replies: consider Falcon-40B-instruct or a 13B with additional retrieval/answer fusion to reduce hallucination.

4) Benchmarks and shared artifacts: we’ll drop the benchmark pack in the shared Drive folder (link below) and open a HubSpot note on deal D-1947 so SDR/AE can track.

Security/ops: SFTP details will be emailed separately (I’ll request secure upload creds from our infra team). For immediate sharing, DocuSign NDA link is fine — you can send it and I’ll route for signature.

Next meeting: propose a 30-minute results sync for Friday Dec 4 (10:00–10:30 PT) to review the smoke eval. Let me know if that works or suggest another slot.

Thanks — we’ll start once your sample CSV is in the SFTP.

Regards,
Nikhil
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
